QF.id: VB Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_15

question.text: Who is the regulator of mutual funds in India?

answer.text: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, SEBI is the regulator of mutual funds in India through the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, which stipulate the legal structure for mutual funds and the obligations of AMCs and trustees. The Trap: The other options (RBI, IRDA, Ministry of Finance directly) are not the regulator of mutual funds. Note: SEBI is also identified in the workbook as the regulator in the investor-grievance and mutual-fund-regulatory context.
